image_cache.keying: The cache is keyed by the decoded source path, so an already-decoded image is served before open() is called; a path redirect never reaches a cached image until it is dropped.
image_cache.module_action: activate() calls lv_image_cache_drop(0) on the UI owner thread after installing the redirect (guarded on both cache globals and their class vtable being non-null), then calls _lv_inv_area (0x0c382428) with an oversized area to mark the whole active screen dirty so the firmware's refresh timer repaints every widget and re-opens each image through the redirect on its next tick, without waiting for a navigation.
image_cache.semantics: Entries are retired ONE AT A TIME with the generic lv_cache_drop (0x0c8b8cae), never with the firmware's drop_all: drop_all frees every red-black node allocation even for still-referenced entries. Per-entry retirement marks a held entry invalid and unlinks it while leaving its payload valid for the holder (deferred free in lv_cache_entry_release_data 0x0c8b9790 on last release); a zero-reference entry is freed immediately. Either way the next lookup for that source path misses and goes through the redirect. NOT established: that every image widget re-opens its source on the next draw — a widget holding a decoded handle across draws keeps showing the old image and needs a page rebuild.

forced_redraw.semantics: Only schedules a repaint through the firmware's own refresh timer (no forced synchronous flush) and does not rebuild pages. One coalesced request is retried from a temporary LVGL timer when the UI is busy (rendering, invalidation disabled, or no active screen yet) and the timer deletes itself on success; this is not periodic polling. Success is counted only when the firmware retained a dirty area covering the whole display. Counted as RHQ1 'redraws' (status format v3, 32 bytes). Timer allocation failure returns -2011 with the redirect left resident.

functions.role: lv_image_cache_drop(src): src=0 drops the decoded-image cache (*0x200bd310) and header cache (*0x200bd314); the module calls this on activate to reload redirected images
LRU-rb drop_all_cb: frees only unreferenced entries, logs still-referenced ones, resets the tree and count

lv_draw_image: per draw calls lv_image_decoder_get_info and (direct branch) lv_image_decoder_open, then lv_image_decoder_close before returning; no decoder is retained across draws. The other branch queues a type-5 draw task via 0x0c380cb8 and is NOT traced

image_decoder_get_info: header-cache (*0x200bd314) lookup; on a hit releases the reference immediately via lv_cache_entry_release_data, on a miss calls lv_fs_open (0x0c3a7d7c) — the hooked driver — and caches the header

lv_image_decoder_open: decoded-image cache (*0x200bd310) lookup; on a hit stores the entry at dsc+68 and holds that reference only until lv_image_decoder_close (0x0c38cf50); on a miss falls through to get_info and the decoder chain

_lv_inv_area: append an area to the display's invalidated-area list (disp+60.., count at disp+604); an oversized area is clipped to the screen, marking the whole display dirty. The module calls this after the image-cache drop to force a full repaint; the firmware's MiWearScreen wake handler (0x0c6d096c) uses it for its 'invalidate screen.' path
lv_display_get_screen_active: returns *(disp+24); confirms the active-screen offset the module's redraw guard reads
lv_display_is_invalidation_enabled: returns disp+608 > 0; _lv_inv_area no-ops when it is 0
Create wrapper: reuse active face, then idle cache, then resolve native path and create FreeType face
Remove one manager wrapper; last reference moves font into idle cache rather than freeing it
Evict idle font: release FreeType cache entry, conditionally drop it, release face pathname, clear/free descriptor, unlink/free idle node
Destroy wrapper and its fallback chain through the global manager
vg_deinit checks live font lists but discards global UI context even if they are nonempty; not an admissible live-UI reload entry
activitymanager_destory_view: only invokes minor-type page callback at offset 100; not whole UI teardown
activitymanager_kill_bg_apps: background apps after home only
miconnect workflow teardown; unrelated to native miwear GUI lifecycle

test_model_boundaries: Exact firmware instructions execute in Unicorn.
Allocator, selected linked-list mutations and native I/O are modeled in font tests.
No physical GPU/display/cache behavior or whole-task shutdown is tested.
No synthetic address in a fixture is a claim about the live heap layout.

physical_probe.probe: newline, then read-only uname -a in separate connection
physical_probe.device_mutations: none; no memory writes, file uploads, task signals or reboot commands

remaining: Fonts: live font wrappers are held by page objects with reference counts; reloading them needs the page-rebuild lifecycle, not a global cache drop, so the module does NOT drop fonts blindly.

Images on screen: the main lv_draw_image path re-opens per draw (traced: get_info/decoder_open/decoder_close), so per-entry retirement plus the full-screen invalidation updates them without a navigation. NOT traced: the deferred type-5 draw-task branch of lv_draw_image, and animation/canvas widgets that own a decoded buffer instead of re-opening a source; those may still need a page rebuild.
Native UI owner scheduling and comprehensive live resource ownership, including persistent default styles and task callbacks.
Path redirection for the native access/FreeType font path, not only LVGL POSIX open.

Forcing an immediate SYNCHRONOUS full redraw: the module now marks the whole screen dirty (_lv_inv_area) but still relies on the firmware's refresh timer to actually flush the repaint; it does not call _lv_display_refr_timer itself.
Working target debug channel and exact firmware identity for live ownership and recovery validation.
